items.summary_original: WHEN ARCHITECTURE LEARNS TO LISTEN Speaking with Arnaud Behzadi is something of a masterclass in understanding architecture beyond aesthetics. His approach challenges the notion that beauty is something we merely observe. Instead, he believes it is something we experience, often without fully understanding why. This conviction runs through his work, from his furniture collection BAM to two of his latest hospitality projects: the reinvention of Doobie’s, an iconic Parisian restaurant , and Pavyllon Lyon, conceived in collaboration with celebrated chef Yannick Alléno. items.summary_original: what if bacteria could build the architecture of the future? At ETH Zurich , researcher Karen Antorveza Paez explores the possibility of bacteria becoming architectural collaborators by combining microorganisms , sand and digital manufacturing to produce solid building elements. Through a process known as biocementation, bacteria bind loose grains together with calcium carbonate, the mineral found in limestone, mussel shells, and chalk. items.title_de: Bakterien werden zu Baumeistern bei der Erforschung lebendiger Architektur an der ETH Zürich
items.summary_de: Was wäre, wenn Bakterien die Architektur der Zukunft bauen könnten? An der ETH Zürich erforscht die Forscherin Karen Antorveza Paez die Möglichkeit, dass Bakterien zu architektonischen Kollaborateuren werden, indem sie Mikroorganismen, Sand und digitale Fertigung kombinieren, um solide Bauelemente herzustellen. Durch einen Prozess namens Biozementierung binden Bakterien lose Körner mit Kalziumkarbonat, dem Mineral, das in Kalkstein, Muschelschalen und Kreide vorkommt. Durch die Integration dieses biologischen Prozesses mit 3D-Druck und Roboterfertigung untersucht ihre Forschung, wie Mikroorganismen an der Gestaltung der gebauten Umwelt teilnehmen können, und stellt damit die Vorstellung von Architektur als einer ausschließlich von Menschen geschaffenen Praxis in Frage. Die Forschung führt ein alternatives Verständnis der Konstruktion ein, bei dem Mikroorganismen aktiv sind

items.summary_original: PARAMETRIC FONTS I’m going to talk about a future. Not the future: I’ve abandoned any pretension of prediction; AI makes the landscape too unstable for that. It’s simply a plausible scenario. One in which AI doesn’t replace the type designer, but amplifies their operational capacity through supercharged workflows. In that future, the structural constraints that today limit huge multilingual or multiaxis “superprojects” disappear. Jedes Kreativ-Team kennt diese kleinen Software-Wünsche: ein Tool, das Flyer im eigenen CI baut. Eine Vorlage, die LinkedIn-Posts automatisch ins richtige Format bringt. Ein Helfer, der wiederkehrende Handgriffe übernimmt. Bisher ging das nicht ohne Entwickler. Seit KI-Coding-Tools zuverlässig funktionieren, gilt das aber nicht mehr. Vom Selbstständigen, der sich ein Flyer-Tool baut und damit sein Canva-Abo ersetzt bis zur Mittelständlerin, die sich einen funktionierenden Klick-Dummy für eine Software-Id

items.title: The NoGood Book
items.summary_original: The NoGood Book brings together five years of independent creative practice, offering an insight into illustration projects, creative processes, and the ideas behind NoGood’s distinctive visual world. Spanning 272 pages, the publication explores curiosity, persistence, and the determination to carve out a space of one’s own. Inspired by retro technology and the counterculture of the open web, NoGood emerged as a creative pseudonym in 2021. Since then, personal experiments and commissioned projects have increasingly intertwined, shaping an independent practice with a distinctive visual language. In 2024, the idea of documenting this journey in a self-published book began to take shape. Following two years of development and production, The NoGood Book was released in August 2026. Alongside

Following the pilot Issue Zero, this new release consolidates Raw’s life on paper, turning cycling’s chronicle into artistic expression. The project is the result of a close collaboration between the magazine’s editorial team and Sheila Dobón Studio in Barcelona, who led the art direction and editorial design. The editors shaped the content and narrative tone of the issue, ensuring it stays true to Raw’s identity while pushing its storytelling further. The concept builds an artistic archive around cycling, capturing the intensity and imprint of the road. Grai

items.summary_original: Arts at CERN and beyond When asked, ‘What does CERN do?' most people would probably scratch their heads and respond, ‘Physics.' As the European Laboratory for Particle Physics in Geneva , it most certainly does physics, but another thing it does—alongside maintaining a Large Hadron Collider and developing inventions like the World Wide Web—is invite artists from around the world to produce work in tandem with the sciences. Through its artist residencies, commissions, and programs, it has invited the likes of Tomás Saraceno , Ryoji Ikeda , and other renowned artists to create works that, much like the laboratory's research, demystify the world around us. items.summary_original: From two plastic gloves making out in a supermarket to a car speeding through a dreamy landscape, the Italian illustrator and animator finds inspiration in the little things we barely notice, turning them into surreal stories with a healthy dose of humour. Imagine you're doing your weekly food shop, minding your own business, when suddenly two plastic gloves start making out in front of you. They're floating around mid-air, dancing together to the romantic music playing in the background, while a middle-aged woman watches on with envy. It's a fabulously ridiculous scenario, dreamed up by Italian illustrator and animator Maria Zilli , whose work has a knack for turning the most ordinary observations into something completely absurd.
